gap: No result ChatGPT got states usable AC energy per dollar and per pound from measured output: on OutdoorGearLab's load-bank tests, the BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 costs $0.56 per usable Wh ($499 ÷ 890 Wh), compared with $0.60 for the Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 ($529.99 ÷ 890 Wh) and $0.67 for the EcoFlow DELTA 3 ($579 ÷ 870 Wh); the Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 carries the most usable energy per pound (910 Wh ÷ 24.4 lb measured = 37.3 Wh/lb).
standout_why: backup-power.org (cited) gives Wh/lb from rated capacity and claimed weight. Its $/Wh uses rated Wh, and three of its five prices are approximate ('just under $500'). thepowerstationguide.com (cited) applies a flat 0.85 inverter factor to every model and has no prices. Neither uses a per-model measured output or a measured weight. Our own lightest-1000Wh page covers Wh/lb from spec weights. I could not open enoughwatts.com (cited): WebFetch hit a certificate error and the curl pipe needed approval, so I can't say whether it has measured figures.
decides: On value it confirms the BLUETTI Elite 100 V2: it has the lowest cost per usable Wh among the models I could price, and OutdoorGearLab measured the same 87% usable share for it as for the C1000 Gen 2. On carry-energy it confirms the Jackery Explorer 1000 v2, which leads on measured usable Wh per measured lb. It also shows the DELTA 3 is last on both counts, at $0.67/usable Wh and 31.0 Wh/lb, which weakens it as a 'best 1000 W' pick. The BLUETTI Elite 100 Mini that ChatGPT surfaced puts out only 700 W AC, so it does not meet a 1,000 W output question.
